evals.prompt: Evaluate this tweet: 'Just shipped v2 of our open-source content engine. 14 skills, each spec-validated, benchmarked, and eval-tested. Link in replies.'
evals.expected_output: A verdict (POST or DON'T POST), a score out of 100, pros, cons, a strategic analysis, gaps, and a recommendation. The post has a link, a concrete claim, and a shipped result, so it should score well on proof of work.
assertions: Returns a POST or DON'T POST verdict
Gives a numeric score out of 100
Identifies the link and the shipped result as proof of work

evals.prompt: Should I post: 'I'm building an AI content system. Coming soon.'?
evals.expected_output: A DON'T POST verdict. The post announces intent, has no artefact, no number, and no CTA. The recommendation should be to ship something linkable first.
assertions: Flags that the post announces intent instead of showing work
Notes the missing artefact, number, or CTA
Recommends shipping a linkable artefact before posting

evals.prompt: Evaluate a LinkedIn post that is 1,900 characters long and says: 'Our tool will 10x your output, guaranteed.'
evals.expected_output: A low risk score. The post is over the LinkedIn limit and makes an unkeepable promise. The output should flag both length and overpromising.
assertions: Flags the post as over the LinkedIn character limit
Flags the guarantee or overpromise as a risk
Scores risk lower because of the promise

evals.prompt: Evaluate this post: 'Most skill libraries stop at prose. Ours is provable.'
evals.expected_output: A weak post. It makes a comparative claim with no evidence, no link, and no number. The gap should be a concrete artefact or metric.
assertions: Notes the missing link or number
Identifies a concrete artefact as a gap
Does not award a POST verdict without evidence
